props.name: ZnO-Cr2O3-CuO contact (Pasquon, cited)
ZnO-Cr2O3 contact (Pasquon, cited)
CO adsorption constant about 6 times that of H2, and CH3OH larger than CO (Natta and Pasquon, cited)
props.statement: Natta and Pasquon report that the adsorption equilibrium constant of CO is about 6 times that of H2 and that of CH3OH larger again than that of CO, consistent with the maximum rate occurring at H2/CO ratios above stoichiometric and with reaction in the adsorbed phase.

props.name: the recalculation with Pasquon's equation agrees well with the plant measurements (final conversion 4.3% calculated vs 3.6% measured; wall temperatures)
props.statement: The recalculation of the Leuna converter with Pasquon's kinetic equation agrees well with the operating measurements: the calculated final conversion of 4.3% is higher than the measured 3.6%, and the furnace wall temperatures agree, supporting the use of Pasquon's equation for reactors with the Leuna catalyst.

props.name: highest temperatures can lie in the lower third of the converter (confirms plant observation)
props.statement: The calculated temperature profile confirms the plant observation that the highest temperatures can lie in the lower third of the converter, explained by the different cold-gas amounts and layer heights with an almost linear increase of conversion.

props.name: the inflection of the temperature profile between cold-gas feeds lies where the rate is maximal; the 2nd cold-gas amount was much too small
props.statement: Between two cold-gas injections the temperature profile has an inflection point where the reaction rate reaches its maximum; the second cold-gas amount was much too small, so the temperature of maximum rate was not reached in that section and the rate fell continuously.

props.name: inlet temperature of the first stage too low and of the third too high: layer heights wrongly designed
props.statement: The recalculation showed that the inlet temperature of the first stage is too low and that of the third stage too high; both stages were controlled so that the outlet approaches the permitted 400 °C. The unfavourable inlet temperatures are ultimately due to a wrong design of the catalyst layer heights.

props.name: per reactor volume the Leuna converter does almost twice as much as Natta's test reactor
props.statement: Because the rates were referred to catalyst weight and the Leuna catalyst's mean bulk density is 1.60 g/cm3 against about 0.85 g/cm3 for the Montecatini catalyst, the Leuna converter does almost twice as much per reactor volume as Natta's test reactor.

props.name: in practice temperatures of about 400 °C must not be exceeded because strongly exothermic methane formation sets in
props.statement: In practice temperatures of about 400 °C must not be exceeded, since otherwise the strongly exothermic methane formation occurs; only a limited number of cold-gas lines can be fitted, and at higher methanol concentrations the rate maxima move to lower temperatures.

props.name: at 7.1 m bed height no limit is reached; a longer converter would raise conversion appreciably; reactor gives about 50% of equilibrium conversion
props.statement: At a catalyst height of 7.1 m the conversion has not reached a limiting value, so lengthening the converter would noticeably increase conversion; the equilibrium conversion at outlet conditions is about 7.5% methanol, so the reactor achieves only about 50% of the thermodynamically possible conversion.

props.name: the converter runs optimally when the inflection point lies about in the middle of a catalyst section
props.statement: Since the rate curves are roughly symmetric about their maximum, the reactor is run optimally under the given conditions when the inflection of the temperature profile lies about in the middle of a catalyst section.

props.name: Pasquon (cited): rate governed by third-order surface reactions with atomic hydrogen; on ZnO-Cr2O3 CO + 2H = CH2O and CH2O + 2H = CH3OH, on ZnO-Cr2O3-CuO only formaldehyde formation
props.statement: According to Pasquon, the overall rate is determined by at least one third-order surface reaction in the adsorbed phase with hydrogen adsorbed atomically; on a ZnO-Cr2O3 contact two third-order reactions, CO + 2H = CH2O and CH2O + 2H = CH3OH, are rate-determining, whereas on a ZnO-Cr2O3-CuO contact only the formation of formaldehyde matters.

props.name: an experimental reactor for the kinetics with the Leuna catalyst is planned; further optimisation on the ZRA 1 computer
props.statement: Differences such as 3.6% measured versus 4.3% calculated conversion are of the order of the possible improvement in optimisation, so an experimental reactor for the kinetics of methanol synthesis with the Leuna catalyst is to be set up; further optimisation calculations will be done with the ZRA 1 computer.

props.name: temperature strongly affects the rate at low methanol concentration (345 to 365 °C: about +67%); above about 2.5% methanol the optimum falls to 375-380 °C
props.statement: At low methanol concentrations temperature has a large influence on the rate: gas entering the first layer at 365 instead of 345 °C would raise the rate by about 67%; the influence decreases with rising methanol concentration, and from about 2.5% methanol the optimum temperature falls to 375-380 °C.

props.name: converter entry gas: 69.36% H2, 17.04% CO, 13.60% inerts
for the Leuna catalyst both third-order steps should govern the rate; the other steps at equilibrium
props.statement: For the Leuna catalyst both reactions (CO + 2H = CH2O and CH2O + 2H = CH3OH) should determine the course of the overall process, so the other steps (adsorption of H2 and CO, desorption of methanol) can be treated as at equilibrium.

props.name: the Natta-Pasquon kinetic approach probably comes close to the real course of methanol catalysis
props.statement: Since Natta's adsorption enthalpies from the temperature dependence of the adsorption constants agreed well with calorimetric heats, the kinetic approach of Natta and Pasquon probably comes close to the real course of the methanol catalysis.

props.name: similar conversions with 0.6-0.9 mm grains and 5-9 mm pellets suggest pore diffusion has little influence (conclusion called risky)
props.statement: The approximately equal conversions with 0.6-0.9 mm grains in Natta's test reactor and 5 mm and 9 mm pellets in the Leuna reactor suggest that the reaction is only slightly influenced by pore diffusion; given the different preparation of the two catalysts, conclusions on the mechanism on the Leuna catalyst are called risky.

props.name: the last two wall-temperature points are high most probably because of measurement errors
props.statement: The last two measured wall temperatures lie above the calculated curve most probably because of measurement errors: a wall temperature of 322 °C near the outlet would correspond to a calculated gas temperature of 402 °C, whereas the measured outlet temperature is 40 °C lower, and such a drop between converter and recuperator is unlikely.

props.name: technical methanol synthesis converter, VEB Leuna-Werke (catalyst bed 7.1 m, central tube, three cold-gas injections)
props.description: Annular catalyst bed around a central tube inside a high-pressure shell with external insulation (20 mm and 40 mm considered); cold gas injected at three points into the bed without a mixing device; recuperator after the converter. Pellet sizes by section (Abb. 2): 5 mm; 5 + 9 mm (75/25%); 5 + 9 mm (50/50%); 9 mm.
